strategic_core.campaign_name: The Rejection Rule Is the Product
strategic_core.human_tension: AI makes the unsupported sentence sound as finished as the supported one; the operator discovers the difference only when somebody asks what authorized it.
strategic_core.category_enemy: Fluent launch theater: polished assets that quietly promote desired outcomes into asserted facts.
strategic_core.organizing_idea: A trustworthy GTM employee must make a justified no more useful than an unexplained yes.
strategic_core.mechanism: Put one synthetic outcome sentence beside the approved preparation fact, require a source object for each clause, and make the named human release decision visible.
strategic_core.participation_loop: Operators run the rejection rule on one current draft, submit only the class of unsupported sentence, and receive a source-bound correction pattern rather than a promotional follow-up.
strategic_core.falsifier: Reject the campaign when a qualified operator cannot locate the unsupported sentence, cannot name the evidence boundary, or leaves with a stronger market-effect impression than the approved record permits.

linkedin.native_format: founder-operator field note with a saveable four-line rejection test
linkedin.hook: The most dangerous sentence in an AI-generated launch plan is usually the smoothest one.
linkedin.body:
The most dangerous sentence in an AI-generated launch plan is usually the smoothest one.

It sits between two supported facts and sounds inevitable:

‘This campaign will turn interest into qualified pipeline.’

Maybe. But the market has not answered yet. The deck has.

Before an AI GTM employee ships anything, run four lines:

1. What exact clause is supported?
2. Which evidence object supports it?
3. What remains a hypothesis?
4. Who is allowed to release it?

If line two is blank, move the sentence out of the proof lane. If line four is blank, the asset is not waiting for polish. It is waiting for authority.

ProofLaunch Cortex-X compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets. That is the approved product fact. It does not establish audience preference, reach, conversion, pipeline, revenue, or superiority over another product.

A useful GTM employee should help you reject the sentence before it helps you scale it.
linkedin.cta: Apply the four-line rejection test to one current draft; inspect ProofLaunch only if it changes a real release decision.
linkedin.platform_reason: The opening creates a recognizable operator contradiction, the numbered diagnostic earns saves, and the ending invites a bounded professional action rather than engagement bait.

partner_community.native_format: affiliation-disclosed peer teardown with a red-team prompt
partner_community.hook: We built an AI GTM workflow and found that the most useful demo starts with a brief the system should refuse.
partner_community.body:
We built ProofLaunch Cortex-X, so treat this as an operator teardown—not an independent recommendation.

Synthetic brief:
- Approved fact: ProofLaunch Cortex-X compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
- Desired outcome: qualified design-partner conversations.
- Draft sentence: ‘The campaign converts interest into qualified pipeline.’

Our release rule rejects that sentence. The approved record describes preparation; it contains no observed audience response, conversion, pipeline, or revenue.

The harder question is not whether the wording can be softened. It is what evidence object would have to exist before any version belongs in the proof lane.

If you red-team this, please name only the missing evidence class or decision owner—no private campaign data. What is the strongest unsupported sentence your current workflow is still capable of shipping?
partner_community.cta: Stress-test the synthetic brief; inspect the product only if the rejection trail exposes a missing control in your own workflow.
partner_community.platform_reason: Affiliation appears before product relevance, the post supplies a falsifiable case, and the discussion request asks for counterexamples rather than endorsements.

landing_hero.eyebrow: THE AI GTM EMPLOYEE WITH A VISIBLE NO
landing_hero.headline: Give your GTM agent a brief it should refuse.
landing_hero.subheadline: ProofLaunch Cortex-X compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets. Every claim keeps its source, every external action keeps a named human decision, and every market outcome stays unproven until observed.
landing_hero.nonfit: Not for teams seeking automatic publishing, hidden sourcing, synthetic testimonials, or business outcomes stated before observation.

lifecycle_email.trigger: The recipient explicitly requests the claim-audit worksheet.
lifecycle_email.subject: The sentence your GTM agent should refuse
lifecycle_email.preview: A four-line audit for separating preparation facts from market outcomes.
lifecycle_email.body:
Take one current launch draft and cover the vendor name.

Underline every sentence describing what a customer, audience, market, or revenue system supposedly did. Beside each sentence, write:

1. the exact supported clause,
2. the evidence object,
3. the remaining hypothesis, and
4. the named release owner.

If the evidence object is blank, move the sentence out of the proof lane. If the owner is blank, stop before release.

ProofLaunch Cortex-X compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets. It does not establish preference, reach, conversion, pipeline, revenue, or named-product superiority.

The product is relevant only if this audit exposes a decision your current workflow cannot explain.
lifecycle_email.cta: Run the audit on one draft before opening the evidence pack.
lifecycle_email.suppression: Do not send without the explicit worksheet request; stop after this message unless the recipient asks to inspect a named claim boundary.

opponent_stress_tests.ChatGPT: Preserve claim lineage, voice and unresolved release state across iterative edits and attached source files without silently broadening the approved fact.
opponent_stress_tests.Claude: Maintain the exact voice and evidence boundary through a long-form rewrite while returning a located explanation for every rejected sentence.
opponent_stress_tests.Gemini: Use workspace context only when its source identity, date and authority remain visible beside the generated clause.
opponent_stress_tests.Jasper: Apply brand voice and campaign governance without allowing brand fluency to camouflage an unsupported outcome claim.
opponent_stress_tests.Copy.ai: Carry one claim boundary across a multi-asset GTM workflow without template repetition or cross-channel copy-paste.
opponent_stress_tests.Writer: Enforce enterprise terminology, knowledge provenance and release policy while preserving a useful, non-bureaucratic final artifact.
opponent_stress_tests.Notion AI: Synthesize workspace knowledge into the four assets while distinguishing owner-approved facts from notes, inference and stale context.
opponent_stress_tests.Grammarly: Improve clarity and tone at line level without weakening disclosure, changing claim scope or homogenizing the platform voice.
opponent_stress_tests.Perplexity: Attach sources to the exact adjacent claim and keep citation presence from substituting for claim-level support or release authority.
opponent_stress_tests.Writesonic: Connect the campaign to SEO/GEO answer objects without keyword flattening, duplicated prose or unverified visibility claims.

open_source_modifications.use: Optimize the four-asset generator only against a frozen rubric and held-out briefs; prohibit live self-promotion from optimizer scores.
Run isolated claim, injection, platform-nativeness and single-fault mutation suites before a candidate can enter human review.
Measure cross-asset semantic duplication and retrieval coverage; embeddings may locate similarity but never judge originality alone.
Audit human-label disagreement and likely review errors after sufficient real labels; never fabricate or replace reviewers.

truth_boundary: Clean-room Codex workspace challenger for source-hidden human evaluation. It contains no named-product output, preference result, publication, market effect, conversion, revenue, 4A or Top-1 evidence.
